next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST (FIN7): a financially driven group that moved from card theft to ransomware ties
next.in_short: GOLD LOCUST is tracked by Secureworks and goes by names including FIN7 and Carbanak. Vendors describe a Russia-origin, profit-driven group that has used mailed USB drives, loaders and security-tool killers, and later ransomware links.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks GOLD LOCUST under the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider and FIN7, and lists Carbanak as its tool.
SentinelOne describes FIN7 as a financially motivated group with origins in Russia.
SentinelOne says that from 2020 the group shifted its focus to ransomware, affiliating with ransomware-as-a-service groups such as REvil and Conti.
S2W reports that Darkside, which it says FIN7 is known to have used, was rebranded as BlackMatter.
FireEye wrote in 2017 that FIN7 kept hitting the restaurant, hospitality and financial services sectors.
An FBI alert, as reported by BleepingComputer, said FIN7 mailed packages through USPS to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 the group hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
SentinelOne lists hospitality, energy, finance, high-tech and retail among the industries that suffered substantial losses.
In the FBI-reported USB campaign, the drives were set up to act as keyboards and fetch GRIFFON malware. The packages used lures such as a gift card.
Malpedia describes Griffon as a small JavaScript implant with no persistence. It receives modules, runs them in memory and sends results to its command servers.
Malwarebytes attributes a late-June malspam campaign that dropped the JSSLoader malware to FIN7.
Morphisec says it has tracked FIN7 (Carbanak Group) for years. It describes a JSSLoader chain, starting with a phishing invoice lure, that ends in the in-memory loading of Carbanak.

SentinelOne assesses with high confidence that several underground forum sellers of antivirus-killer tools belong to the FIN7 cluster. It describes one of these tools, AvNeutralizer, as tampering with security products.
SentinelOne attributes automated SQL injection intrusions to FIN7 with medium confidence. It says it cannot conclusively tell whether LockBit intrusions using AvNeutralizer were run by FIN7.
Harfanglab says the developers of the PackXOR packer might be connected to the FIN7 cluster. It adds that the packer appears to be used for activity unrelated to FIN7.
SentinelLABS reported in November 2022 that Black Basta ransomware attacks deployed custom EDR evasion tools it ties to FIN7.

The Hacker News, citing NCC Group, reported in December 2023 that Carbanak was being used in ransomware attacks. The installers impersonated business software such as HubSpot, Veeam and Xero and were hosted on compromised websites.
Treat unexpected USB drives and unsolicited software installers as suspect, and protect security tools against tampering.
